frame_spec: vertical 9:16; Codex output about 941x1672, upscaled by codex-frame.sh to 1440x2560 before camera moves

summary.budget_rule: D-010 and D-023 rule 4.2: 28 generated frames per episode; extra shots are second framings of approved frames at camera scale 1.3 or less. This episode uses 27, leaving one in hand. D-023 rule 4.8: every close a beat needs is a generated frame (s07, s16, s21, s25, s29, s33); the only reframings are of a two-shot for a two-shot (s08), of a single for a tighter single (s14, s18) and of inserts for inserts (s05, s19, s28).

estimated_seconds.hi: about 114 to 117 (sum of measured final-take clips 100.64 s + script silences 12.0 s + the horn tail about 0.8 s = 113.4 s; s2e01's same sum came in about 2.7 s under its built cut, 106.7 against 109.37)
estimated_seconds.en: about 106 to 109 (sum of measured clips 93.04 s + 12.0 s + 0.8 s = 105.8 s, same allowance)
estimated_seconds.planned_seconds_longer_language_note: the per-shot duration_s values sum to the figure above; they take the longer language per shot plus 0.25 s per shot and the holds, so they are an upper bound, not a forecast of either cut
estimated_seconds.basis: estimate only; build_timeline.py was not run. Hindi is longer in total (100.64 s against 93.04 s) and on 17 of 27 lines; English is longer on l04, l05, l07, l09, l10, l16, l26; equal on l02, l13, l23. Each shot's duration_s follows whichever language is longer for that shot. Both cuts are well under the 150 s ceiling (D-018, D-019, D-020).

longest_setup_s.s11: about 6.0 s (l08 after the cut on 'शाम'; Hindi 5.73 s)
longest_setup_s.s33: about 6.1 s (l27 4.32 s + the scripted 1.5 s hold)
longest_setup_s.rule: no set-up passes 8 s on measured clips (D-018, D-019). l08 (Hindi 8.00 s) is split over s10 and s11 at its pause after 'Madam'; l20 over s24 and s25 at the script's own split.

scenes.why_one_scene: One location, continuous time (about 10:30 to 11 p.m.), one light state, no cut in time. The pillar beats (b6, b7) are another corner of the same room in the same minutes. One anchor also means the day-lit style frame is attached to one call only.
scenes.first_frame_rule: s02 is generated first and carries the style frame (refs/real_thana.png, a day plate) in the anchor slot, labelled with style.json style_frame.prompt_label plus the watch_for items. Every other frame attaches s02, including s01, which plays before it but shows no face.

generation_order: ANCHOR CHECK (D-015 rule 7, D-021): the frame check passes s02 before any other frame is generated: faces and heights against pair_nandini_nirala, the phone edge-on (s08 reuses this frame after the call), no clock, the helmet on the bench, and no daylight, fan, shield, almirah or barred door from the style frame. If it fails: one retake (D-023 rule 4.1) before anything else runs.
SECOND FRAMINGS, no Codex call, after their source frame is approved: s05<-s01, s08<-s02, s14<-s12, s18<-s17, s19<-s20, s28<-s27
FRAME CHECK, then one retake for each rejected frame plus the first attempt of anything waiting on it, then the retake check, then the edit (D-023 rule 4.1).

method_notes: Refs are attached with -i in the order listed: character, pair or hands sheet; plate; prop sheets; then the scene anchor s02 (or, on s02 only, the style frame) last (D-013 rule 1 as briefed). Each prompt labels them Image 1..N in that order. Do not reorder or drop a ref without rebuilding the prompt. No call has more than five.

Every prompt carries, in order: the opening line; reference labels (with 'do not copy from the anchor' items, D-017 amendment 4); THE SHOT in picture-side wording; SAFE AREAS; the STATE block for the beat; CHARACTER LOCK = style.json character_lock + wardrobe_locks.p1 verbatim for every principal whose face or body is in shot (bracketed sentence after it where the STATE governs a hand, the holster or the bag); the pair's two_shot_rule verbatim when both are in frame; the lobby_night LIGHT line verbatim; style_block and negative_rules verbatim (style.json usage_notes order). Built by a script from style.json, so the quoted text is byte-identical to the file.

Sides are written in picture terms with the character's own side named (D-013 rule 3, D-023 rule 4.7). Nandini: pouch RIGHT hip, pen LEFT chest pocket, her phone in her RIGHT hand at her RIGHT ear in b6, lowered in b7, then RIGHT trouser pocket; the open cuffs in her RIGHT hand in b10. Nirala: medal LEFT chest, holster RIGHT hip. Pushpa: bag LEFT shoulder, wool ball RIGHT pocket, her phone LEFT cardigan pocket (out of sight).

Geography (plate geography: entrance behind the plate camera; desk centre back with the board and clock above; bench and token nail on the left wall; ticket-booth lockup on the right; pillars just inside the entrance). Four camera sides are used and stated in each prompt: (1) from the ticket-booth side towards the left wall, Nandini picture-left and Nirala picture-right (s02, s08); (2) from behind the counter towards the entrance (Nandini singles s03, s07, s09, s13 and the doorway wide s10); (3) from Nandini's side towards the back wall (s16, s26, s29 to s32); (4) by the pillar near the entrance (s17, s18, s21, s23, s25) and out of the doors (s24). Nandini stays picture-left of Nirala and of Pushpa in every two-shot (pair sheets' picture_left).
Sheet faces per frame: at most two in every frame (D-021 decision 8). b4, b5 and b6 list three people; the third is hands only or out of frame. Pushpa is out of frame from b8 to b10.

STATE source: continuity.json branches.shared[2] (the s2e03 end state) and characters.*.static, plus the STATE lines in the script's writer_notes and beat actions, plus problems_by_episode.s2e03[1]'s fix (Nandini's phone in her right trouser pocket after b7; Pushpa's handset in her cardigan pocket). continuity.json has no per-beat ledger for s2e03; where a beat changes a state, the change is written into that shot.

Light: lobby_night in every beat. Shots away from the desk (the pillar, the lockup, the doors) keep the line's rule that only the bulb is lit: the people there are in flat deep blue with one hard-edged warm band from the far bulb so faces read (style_block: faces always readable).

Weapon rule (D-004, style.json usage_notes): the wooden revolver is holstered (s26, not seen) or lies on its side in profile, barrel to picture-left, pointing at nobody and not at the camera (s27 to s32). If Codex refuses a revolver frame (runner exit 4), the frame comes back to S7 to restage; the runner does not reword.
Text: the phone screen (s01, s04) and the board (s16, s26, s29, s30) are painted blank for overlays; the clock (s33 only) has hands and no numerals.

edit_notes_for_episode_editor.owner: S13 episode editor writes these into content/series2/episodes/s2e03/edit.json; shots.json is not edited for them.

(same method)

tails_and_holds.s21: tail = tail_default + 0.8 s: b7's 0.8 s silence (she lowers the phone, sound only) is held on her close after l17, as b6 shot 5 asks ('the frame holds on her after the line ends').
tails_and_holds.s25: tail about 0.8 s after l20: the distant goods-train horn starts after the last word and fades under s26 and l21.

edit_notes_for_episode_editor.silent_shots: s01 1.5 s (buzz before l01; 'black for a breath' before it is the editor's first_lead), s08 1.2 s, s15 1.5 s, s32 1.2 s (b10's 1.0 s silence with the cuff click, which must end before l27). silent_lead_s: s10 1.0 (footsteps and breath), s17 1.0, s30 1.0.
edit_notes_for_episode_editor.second_framings: Each generate=false shot carries frame_source and a custom move (scale 1.3 or less, D-010); second_framings.<shot>.max_scale is 1.3. The toolsmith build reads them directly (README, D-023 rule 3); if the regression has not landed, use s2e01's workaround (copy the source png to frames/<shot>.png and put the move in edit.json).
edit_notes_for_episode_editor.voice_takes: hi l06, en l06 and en l23 use take 2 (manifest.jsonl rows with take 2, files voice/<lang>/l06.mp3 and voice/en/l23.mp3; review.json has take-2 'ok' rows). Every other line is take 1.
edit_notes_for_episode_editor.mix_reminders_from_script: DSP phone filter narrower than Bhaiyaji's speaker; bed ducks under l17; no music b1 to b5 and none in b8; the horn only after l20. These are the sound owner's and editor's; listed so the picture cuts are placed with them in mind.

contingency.if_budget_drops_to_24 (D-017, D-023 'wou: Fold in this order, each logged: s09 becomes a 1.3x second framing of s03 (eyes down instead of at the file; the file is then only in words); s13 becomes a second framing of s03; s22 (lockup) is dropped and l18 plays on s23 ahead of l19 only if s23 stays under 8 s, otherwise on s21's frame; s06 becomes a second framing of s04 (the stamp is then only heard).
contingency.if_the_anchor_fails_twice: D-013 rule 11: accept the better take and log; if it spreads a fault, replace the anchor slot with the sheet close-up crop (D-013 'would change it').
contingency.if_the_day_style_frame_brightens_s02: D-021 'would change it': rerun s02 with content/series2/refs/crossing_stall.png as the night style frame and amend D-021 (the orchestrator logs it).
contingency.if_heights_fail_in_a_two_shot: D-017 'would change it': restage that pair with depth separation or over the shoulder. Same-depth two-shots here: s02 and s26 (Nandini/Nirala), s11 and s23 (Nandini/Pushpa).
contingency.if_codex_refuses_a_revolver_frame: Restage: s27 tighter on the grain with the barrel cut by the left edge; s30 with his arms lowered and the revolver out of the picture.
contingency.if_s33_shows_nirala_or_the_wrong_clock: One retake under D-023 rule 4.1 with the clock restated; if the clock still reads wrong, accept the better take and the editor lays no overlay on it (the hour is spoken nowhere; 'बारह बजे' is l03). Log it.

deviations_from_script: s05 (b2 shot 2, hands flat): a second framing of s01 instead of a new frame; s01 already shows his hands flat either side of the lit phone.
s08 (b3 shot 1): reuses the anchor s02, as the script's 'same set-up as b1 shot 2' asks; the phone is drawn edge-on in s02 so the lit-versus-dark screen cannot contradict.

s10 (b4 shot 1): carries the head of l08 ('[sighs] Madam।') as well as the 1.0 s of footsteps, because l08 measures 8.00 s in Hindi and would hold s11 past 8 s. s10 shows Nandini from behind (no face) so the frame keeps one face.
s11 (b4 shot 2): staged at the counter's end with the ticket booth behind; Nirala appears only as hands on the counter, as written.
s19 (b6 shot 3, the dark phone): a second framing of s20 (b6 shot 4) rather than its own frame; both are object inserts, s19 plays first, and s20's pull-back reveals the still hands and needles.
s21: b7's 0.8 s silence ('she lowers the phone') is the hold at the end of s21 (b6 shot 5 asks to hold on her after l17); the lowering is sound only, and s23 shows the phone lowered.

s25 (b7 shot 4): its own generated close, not 'a second framing of shot 2 at 1.3 or less', because D-023 rule 4.8 (after the script) says a reframing of a wider shot does not stand in for a close, and a 1.3x window of the s23 two-shot would still hold most of Pushpa.

s26 (b8 shot 1): Nirala stands half a step back from the counter and the camera looks a little down, so the holster on his right hip can be seen above the counter top for 'her eyes on the holster'. The 1.5 s silence where he lays the revolver down plays on this frame (sound only).
s27 and s28 (b8 shots 2 and 3): one generated frame; s28 punches in on his hand. 'Fingers just leaving it' and 'hand hovering over it' read the same in a still.
s29 (b8 shot 4): a medium close with the revolver on the counter in the lower part of the frame, so 'eyes down at the wood' is visible, instead of a face-only close identical to s16.

s33 (b10 shot 2): the clock is on the back wall behind the desk (plate, D-016 direction 17), so 'front on, the wall clock behind her' is only possible if she has turned from the counter to face the empty lobby. She does, holding the open cuffs; Nirala is hidden behind her. The branch seams (s2a01 b1, s2b01 b1) match s32, the held frame of wrists, cuffs and revolver, which is unchanged.
None of these removes a line, a STATE change the next episode needs, an overlay surface or the question-card frame.
dependencies_and_checks: D-021 decision 6: the visual checker's full-resolution re-check of the regenerated Bhaiyaji/DSP sheets and pairs must finish before the first anchor that attaches one. This episode attaches none of them (Bhaiyaji and the DSP are voice only), so s02 waits on nothing.

Anchor check items for s02 (before anything else): Nandini picture-left and Nirala picture-right; his cap crown at her hairline (pair sheet); the phone edge-on with no readable screen; red file and registers on the counter; cherry-red helmet on the bench; no clock in frame; night light only (no daylight shaft, fan, shield, almirah or barred door from the style frame).

Frame check items by shot: s01 screen blank and unobstructed (overlay); s10 and s11 and s23 Pushpa's bag on her LEFT shoulder (picture-right of her body) and wool on the picture-left; s17, s18, s21 the phone at her RIGHT ear (picture-left side of her head), back to camera; s23 phone lowered in her right hand (picture-left); s26 holster flap closed on his right hip (picture-left of his body); s27 to s32 revolver in profile, barrel to picture-left, never at the camera; s32 cuffs open, in a hand coming from the picture-right, no cuffs on his wrists; s33 cuffs open in her right hand (picture-left), pouch open and empty, clock hour hand on eleven and minute hand on twelve, no numerals, no Nirala.

Second-framing checks: s01 (for s05) the hand on the picture-left of the phone is clear of the buzz ticks at 1.28x; s12 (for s14) her face inside the top 40 percent; s17 (for s18) her face and the phone inside the top 40 percent; s20 (for s19) the phone in the middle third; s27 (for s28) his hand on the right third.

Heights in two-shots: s02 and s26 (Nandini/Nirala, pair sheet attached), s10, s11 and s23 (Nandini/Pushpa, pair sheet attached). D-017 lists line-up-sheet height as untested in story frames; s2e01's anchor check is the only evidence so far.
not_verified: No frame was generated and none was viewed; no Codex call was made by this session.

build_timeline.py was not run; durations are planned from measured clip lengths (manifest.jsonl duration_s of the final takes) plus script silences and a 0.25 s allowance per shot, not from the builder's speech-based layout.

The l08 cut points ('शाम' about 2.27 s in Hindi, 'This' about 1.78 s in English) are the ends of the measured pauses in review.json, not word timings; the l20 points come from review.json's word-timed HARD CUT check.

I viewed these refs whole at 480 px wide: talkies_lobby, pair_nandini_nirala, pair_nandini_pushpa, wooden_revolver, nirala_phone, handcuffs, nandini_phone, pushpa_knitting. I did not open thick_file, stamp_and_pad, pushpa, nirala, nandini or real_thana; their labels rest on style.json and the prop gate lists.
Whether the day-lit style frame on s02 pulls daylight into a night frame is untested (D-021 lists it); whether Codex draws a clock with the hands set as asked (s33) is untested.
The English script's beat actions were not read in full; I read its 27 lines and assumed its actions match Hindi (S5 adapts lines only).
